questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code computes the per-device average while readings are still arriving? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two MQTT threads receive the first readings for the same device and minute at the same moment. What does record() guarantee?
choices: One thread may get a null Bucket and throw a NullPointerException
Each thread creates its own Bucket and the last put wins
Both threads add to the same Bucket instance, because computeIfAbsent creates at most one value per key
The two threads are serialized for the entire record() call

questions.prompt: A reading stamped three hours and ten minutes ago arrives after the sweeper has already run for that period. What happens?
choices: It creates a new bucket containing only that reading, which the next sweep removes
It is added to the old bucket that was kept alive by the retention window
It is rejected by record() because the bucket no longer exists
It throws because evictOlderThan has frozen the map

questions.prompt: A device publishes the payload "sensor-7,21500,abc". What does onMessage() do?
choices: Propagates a NumberFormatException to the MQTT client thread
Records the temperature but skips the timestamp bucket
Records nothing, increments the dropped counter and returns normally
